title: Steak Bites with Sweet Potato Fries

items: 1 lb top sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1½ lb), scrubbed and cut into ½-inch-thick sticks
1 jalapeño, stemmed, seeded and roughly chopped
½ cup packed fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.

Pat the sweet potato sticks dry. In a bowl, toss them with the cornstarch until lightly dusted, then add the oil, paprika and salt and toss again. Spread them on the pan in a single layer with space between; use 2 pans if crowded.
Bake 25–30 min, flipping once halfway, until browned at the edges and tender inside. Let them sit on the pan 3–5 min to crisp.
While the fries bake, blend the ranch, jalapeño and cilantro until smooth and pale green. Chill until serving.
Pat the steak cubes dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke.
Add the steak in a single layer, in 2 batches if needed. Sear 1–2 min without moving, until a brown crust forms, then turn and cook 1–2 min more.

Return all the steak to the pan and lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and garlic and toss 1 min, until the garlic is fragrant and the steak is coated. Check a cube: 130–135°F for medium-rare, 140–145°F for medium.
Serve the steak bites with the fries and green dip.
tips: Air fryer fries: cook at 400°F for 14–18 min in a single layer, shaking the basket halfway.
Leave the jalapeño seeds in if you want the dip spicier.
storage: Steak and fries keep 3 days in the fridge, the dip 4 days. Re-crisp the fries in the air fryer at 400°F or the oven at 425°F for 4–6 min. Warm the steak in a skillet over medium heat 1–2 min so it doesn't overcook.
